headline: Clayface Director Addresses Future Of The Character
post:
The DCU's first R-rated horror movie, Clayface, is currently proving popular with audiences and holds an impressive audience score on Rotten Tomatoes.

However, director James Watkins recently revealed in an interview that he viewed the project as a standalone film and directed it as such. He noted that any future plans for the character will ultimately be up to James Gunn.

Do you hope to see a sequel to Clayface, or do you feel it's better to leave a successful movie alone?

#Clayface #JamesWatkins #DCU
original_title: Clayface Director Addresses What’s Next For The Character & It’s Probably Not a Sequel

headline: Spider-Man joins the new Avengers lineup
post:
Hey superhero friends! According to Screen Rant, comic readers have a massive month ahead with several exciting storylines rolling out. In Marvel's Armageddon, Captain America is out of his coma, and a brand new roster steps up to protect the world. This lineup features Spider-Man alongside Wolverine, Daredevil, Luke Cage, Captain Marvel, and Miracleman. Meanwhile, Spider-Man also faces off separately against the Infernal Hulk in another major showdown.

Over in DC Comics, Tom King's Wonder Woman approaches its final issues with the future at stake as the Sovereign and the Sisters of Fate return. Plus, in Transformers #38, the terrifying Megatronus Rex is finally revealed following his pupa stage after being announced at the 2026 New York Comic-Con. Shredder also takes on a brand new leadership role running the Earth Protection Force with fear as a motivator.

Which of these epic comic book issues are you grabbing first?

headline: Man-Thing's Surprising Debut in Savage Tales
post:
Did you know Marvel’s terrifying muck monster actually made his very first appearance in a sword-and-sorcery magazine called Savage Tales back in the 1970s? It is such an unexpected piece of comic book history for a modern horror character to debut there.

From crossing paths with major heroes to helping introduce Howard the Duck, Man-Thing had quite a wild Bronze Age run before landing in the MCU's Werewolf by Night special!

headline: Cillian Murphy's Scarecrow holds unique Batman record
post:
Did you know that Cillian Murphy's Jonathan Crane holds a very special place in DC cinematic history? According to /Film, the character earned a unique record by appearing across Christopher Nolan's entire "Dark Knight" trilogy without a single recast or reboot. That is three consecutive movies as the terrifying fear-toxin dealer! 🦇

Even though the Joker, Catwoman, the Riddler, and the Penguin take the crown for most overall appearances, Scarecrow is the only villain to achieve this specific consecutive streak in the live-space. Despite this cool milestone, Cillian Murphy's version always served as a subordinate or foil rather than stepping into the absolute lead role.

Fans can even spot Murphy's lasting legacy in recent comics like "Absolute Batman," where the latest iteration of the character sports a style reminiscent of both Crane and Oppenheimer! What is your favorite Scarecrow moment from the trilogy? 🎃

#CillianMurphy #Batman #DCComics
original_title: Cillian Murphy's Scarecrow Holds A Unique Record Among Batman Movie Villains
